result.rationale: The diff shows parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full SafeParseReturn (`return refreshTokenResponse;` where refreshTokenResponse is schema.safeParse(result)). In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` is then passed directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, storing the {success, data} envelope as the credential key instead of key.data, breaking subsequent googleCredentialSchema validation for all deployments.

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full zod SafeParseReturn ({success, data}) and Google stores that envelope directly as the credential key (data: { key }) instead of the parsed key.data. After the first token refresh, credential.key becomes {success: true, data: {...}} and no longer matches googleCredentialSchema, so the next attempt to construct GoogleCalendarService fails schema validation — Google Calendar breaks for every deployment (sharing enabled or not), not just credential-sharing ones.

After the first token refresh, credential.key becomes {success: true, data: {...}} and no longer matches googleCredentialSchema, so the next attempt to construct GoogleCalendarService fails schema validation — Google Calendar breaks for every deployment (sharing enabled or not), not just credential-sharing ones.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (a `SafeParseReturn` with `{ success, data }`) rather than the parsed value (`.data`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the returned value is assigned to `key` and persisted directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, meaning the stored credential key becomes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` instead of the expected credential payload shape. This is inconsistent with how other call sites use it (e.g., Office365 spreads `tokenResponse.data`). This would corrupt the stored credential key format after refresh and likely break subsequent uses expecting the schema shape.
